scope: Three opponent catches from one bounded live window; not a general win-rate estimate.

nativeStamina.conclusion: The WR 75-stamina opening assumption does not explain these DB cases. All three DB cases began with 100.

coverageReversal.fix: Use a 1e-6 tolerance on normalized Z only when selecting the existing goal-side coverage turn. Turn rate and genuine backward/noncoverage behavior stay unchanged.
coverageReversal.limitation: Private steering state is not recorded. The observed backward arc is consistent with this reproduced edge case, but the incident does not prove it was the sole live cause.

openingAlignment.oldGates: Wide lateral emergency required more than 6 yards; the smaller lateral-cut trigger required fast outward velocity. A receiver already turning upfield at ordinary speed could leave a large opening alignment gap with neither trigger active.
unchanged: Native run speed 20 and sprint speed 27
Postthrow catch geometry and server claims

case8CatchGeometrySensitivity.limitation: These are planner geometry counterfactuals using the same throw and authored native-like configuration. They do not establish an executable recovery path, native collision behavior, or an awarded catch.

remainingCases.observation: Late sideways cut occurred outside the opening window. The new opening rule does not change the replayed coverage decisions. No postthrow jump/dive was omitted from a feasible catch plan.

Receiver retreated before throwing. The DB retained goal-side depth, then chased at normal speed; no catch plan was feasible from the recorded throw geometry. Opening changes do not claim to fix this distinct late retreat. Post-catch tackle was reviewed separately.

verification.testCoverage: The existing91 retained cases and both new policy cases passed. The new cases are also in the normal public defensive suite, which passed18/18.

limitations: Offline policy replay reproduces logged inputs, not full native physics or the opponent reacting to changed movement.
A changed sprint request is not proof of native sprint acceptance, recovered catch, or prevented touchdown.
No server catch/tackle rejection reason was available.
No claim of perfect defense or zero future incompletes.
privacy: No player names, account identifiers, credentials, extracted game source, or machine paths.
